blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — bronchoscope/endoscope reprocessing and high-level disinfection
stem: A reusable flexible bronchoscope has just been used for a client. Which reprocessing approach is required before the bronchoscope is used again?

options.A: Clean the bronchoscope's external surfaces and internal channels thoroughly, then perform at least high-level disinfection before the next use.
options.B: Perform high-level disinfection first, then brush and flush the internal channels afterward to remove material loosened during disinfection.
options.C: Clean and disinfect the exterior thoroughly, then flush the internal channels with water because the channels do not require high-level disinfection.
options.D: Clean all external surfaces and internal channels thoroughly, then use low-level disinfection when the previous client had no known infection.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC guidance states that heat-sensitive endoscopes, including bronchoscopes, must be properly cleaned and at minimum undergo high-level disinfection after each use. CDC also specifies that meticulous cleaning must precede high-level disinfection and that cleaning includes the external surfaces and internal channels. B reverses the required sequence because cleaning must occur before high-level disinfection. C leaves the internal channels without the required high-level disinfection. D uses an inadequate disinfection level; reprocessing requirements do not depend on whether the previous client had a known infection.
educational_objective: Reprocess a reusable flexible bronchoscope by meticulous cleaning of external surfaces and internal channels followed by at least high-level disinfection before reuse.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Disinfection of Healthcare Equipment — Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC healthcare-equipment guidance dated November 28, 2023 and live-currentness rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Disinfection of Healthcare Equipment lines 37-42: heat-sensitive endoscopes including bronchoscopes must be properly cleaned and at minimum high-level disinfected after each use. Lines 58-65: meticulous cleaning must precede high-level disinfection. Lines 74-79: cleaning includes external surfaces and brushing/flushing internal channels, followed by high-level disinfection with disinfectant perfused through accessible channels.
source_claim_supported: CDC directly supports cleaning a reusable flexible bronchoscope after each use, cleaning both external surfaces and internal channels before disinfection, and performing at least high-level disinfection before reuse.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and use equipment safely to prevent transmission and protect clients and health care personnel.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — the official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; CDC evidence used for the clinical key is current HTML, not PDF.

option_audit.A: Correct; includes external and internal cleaning before at least high-level disinfection.
option_audit.B: Plausible sequencing error; incorrect because meticulous cleaning must precede high-level disinfection.
option_audit.C: Plausible partial reprocessing approach; incorrect because accessible internal channels also require high-level disinfection, not water flushing alone.
option_audit.D: Plausible risk-stratified shortcut; incorrect because at least high-level disinfection is required after each use regardless of known infection status.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths are balanced: A 143, B 140, C 149, D 142 characters; the key is not uniquely longest.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on an obvious all/only/always/never cue.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified: B reverses sequence, C underprocesses internal channels, and D uses an inadequate disinfection level.
